source_name: EKR - Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (portal)
why_relevant: Legally mandated national e-procurement platform (operational since 2018, Kbt. + 424/2017 Korm. rendelet). All Hungarian contracting authority procedures — including bank account management, card acceptance/POS, cash handling and core-banking IT — are conducted and documented here. Primary spine for A2 tender/award intelligence.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Public Procurement Bulletin) - Közbeszerzési Hatóság
why_relevant: Official gazette of the Public Procurement Authority publishing every domestic notice: ajánlati/ajánlattételi felhívás, tájékoztató az eljárás eredményéről (award notice), szerződésmódosítás, teljesítés. Below-EU-threshold banking/payments contracts appear here and nowhere else.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság - Hirdetmény adatbázis (structured notice search)
why_relevant: Field-level searchable notice database behind the Értesítő — filter by contracting authority, notice type, CPV and date. The most collection-friendly entry point for systematic banking/payments CPV sweeps.

source_name: CoRe - Szerződésnyilvántartó rendszer (public contract register), publikus kereső
why_relevant: Statutory register of public procurement CONTRACTS concluded since 1 Jan 2018, with contract text, value, parties and modifications. Turns award notices into actual contract terms/values for banking and payment-services deals — the layer notices alone do not give.

source_name: KBA - Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (legacy pre-2018 procedures and contracts)
why_relevant: Historical archive of procedures and contracts before the EKR/CoRe cut-over (pre-2018). Needed to reconstruct multi-cycle history of bank account-management and card-acceptance mandates, which typically run on 3-5 year cycles.

source_name: Hirdetményfigyelő (official Authority notice-alert service)
why_relevant: Official saved-search/alerting layer on the Értesítő. Lets the intelligence programme receive push notification of new banking/payments notices instead of relying on polling, with authoritative provenance.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság - döntőbizottsági és bírósági határozatok kereső
why_relevant: Remedy-body and court decisions on contested procurements. Reveals competitive dynamics invisible in notices: who challenged a bank-account or POS tender, on what grounds, disqualifications, annulled awards, and specification disputes.

source_name: Nyilvántartott ajánlatkérők (register of contracting authorities)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map: the full list of entities legally obliged to procure under Kbt. Used to build the target universe (ministries, municipalities, state holdings, utilities) whose banking/payments contracts must eventually be tendered.

source_name: Minősített ajánlattevők jegyzéke (qualified bidders list)
why_relevant: Supply-side map: which vendors are pre-qualified to bid. Combined with Kizárt ajánlattevők (excluded bidders) and Szerződésszegések (contract breaches) it profiles the competitive field around payments/IT contracts.

source_name: TED - Tenders Electronic Daily (Hungary, above-threshold notices)
why_relevant: All Hungarian procurements above EU thresholds are also published in the OJEU supplement. TED offers structured eForms XML, bulk downloads and a search API — often the cleanest machine-readable route to the same HU banking/payments notices carried by the Értesítő.

source_name: KEF Központosított Közbeszerzési Portál (kozbeszerzes.gov.hu)
why_relevant: KEF is the designated central purchasing body for government institutions; framework agreements (keretmegállapodás) it signs cover IT, telecom and office categories that can carry payment-terminal, cash-handling and banking-IT scope. Institutions buy through this portal rather than running their own tenders — a major channel that would be missed by watching EKR alone.

source_name: DKÜ Zrt. - Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség, IT procurement portal (IDPR)
why_relevant: DKÜ holds exclusive competence over state IT procurement (301/2018 Korm. rendelet; unified IDPR portal since 1 Jan 2025, reinforced by 467-468/2025 decrees). Core-banking IT, payment software and terminal-related state purchases route through DKÜ framework agreements, making it a second mandatory choke point alongside EKR.

source_name: OpenTender.eu - Hungary dataset (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Cleaned, structured OCDS-style dataset combining TED with the Hungarian national portal, explicitly including below-EU-threshold Hungarian contracts. Gives bulk historical analytics (award values, buyer-supplier networks) far faster than scraping notices, and serves as a cross-check on own collection completeness.

source_name: Red Flags (redflags.eu) - K-Monitor / Transparency International Hungary / PetaByte
why_relevant: Algorithmic risk-flagging of Hungarian procurement notices; useful for spotting single-bidder, tailored-spec or rushed banking/payments tenders. Reported as not updated since 27 October 2023 due to TED data-source changes — valuable as a historical corpus and methodology reference rather than a live feed.

source_name: Tender-Értesítő (tender-ertesito.hu) - commercial notice monitoring
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator covering Közbeszerzési Értesítő, TED and additional Hungarian buyer portals, with keyword alerting and a free trial. Useful as a completeness cross-check and to surface non-Kbt. buyer notices that never reach EKR.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hirdetmény Figyelő (khf.hu)
why_relevant: Aggregates Közbeszerzési Értesítő + TED + additional Hungarian buyer sourcing pages into one searchable database; an alternative commercial cross-check with different coverage of non-Kbt. buyer notices.

source_name: TenderMonitor (kozbeszerzesmonitor.hu) / Napitender / InnoTender - HU monitoring vendors
why_relevant: Cluster of Hungarian tender-monitoring vendors covering all national and EU sources with unlimited-keyword subscriptions. Relevant mainly as coverage benchmarks and as a shortcut to keyword taxonomies that Hungarian bidders actually use for banking/payments lots.

source_name: Tender Help Hungary - EKR/procurement explainer (EN+HU)
why_relevant: Bilingual practitioner explainer of EKR mechanics, notice types and tendering interfaces. Useful for building the HU/EN glossary and understanding how to navigate EKR search — not a data source itself.

source_name: EKR user manual (Felhasználói Kézikönyv) - PDF
why_relevant: Documents EKR's data model, notice types, search fields and identifiers (EKR eljárásazonosító). Essential engineering reference for designing a reliable EKR collector and for mapping HU notice-type names to a normalised schema.

source_name: Új Világ Nonprofit Szolgáltató Kft. - EKR operator information pages
why_relevant: Operator-side pages for EKR, including system information and planned full-refresh/maintenance windows. Operationally important for scheduling collection so maintenance pages are not mistaken for dead endpoints.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság - statisztikák és éves beszámolók
why_relevant: Official statistical service and annual reports of the Authority give aggregate market volumes by CPV/sector, letting banking/payments procurement be sized and trended without parsing every notice.

source_name: GVH közbeszerzési kartell döntések (Competition Authority procurement cartel decisions)
why_relevant: Competition-authority decisions on procurement cartels reveal supplier collusion patterns and market structure in tendered categories, including IT/terminal supply chains relevant to payments.

source_name: Buyer-side 'Közérdekű adatok / Közbeszerzés' disclosure pages (e.g. BKV, municipal institutions)
why_relevant: Individual contracting authorities must publish their procurement plans (közbeszerzési terv), contracts and non-Kbt. procurements ('nem közbeszerzés') on their own sites. These carry below-threshold banking, cash-handling and terminal purchases that never enter the Értesítő, and publish procurement plans months before notices appear — the earliest lead signal available.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (Supplement to the Official Journal of the EU)
source_subtype: official EU procurement gazette / notice database
why_relevant: All above-threshold Hungarian public contracts (incl. banking, payment, card acquiring, ATM, cash handling and IT-for-banking services bought by ministries, municipalities, state-owned banks and utilities) must be published EU-wide here. Gives structured, multilingual, machine-readable duplicates of national notices, including contract notices, award notices (with winner and value) and modifications.

source_name: TED Search API (TED Developer Docs)
why_relevant: Documented, authentication-free API for querying published notices with expert query syntax and retrieving notices in XML. This is the operational backbone for a repeatable HU banking/payments tender feed rather than manual browsing.

source_name: TED XML bulk download packages (daily / monthly)
why_relevant: Full daily/monthly archives of all TED notices in XML permit backfilling a multi-year Hungarian banking/payments tender history and computing incumbency, contract values and renewal cycles — impossible via the web UI.

source_name: eForms SDK documentation (OP-TED)
why_relevant: Defines the eForms schema, field IDs and codelists now used for all Hungarian notices sent to TED. Needed to parse notices correctly (lot structure, CPV, estimated value, award winner, framework agreement flags) and to build stable extraction rules.
